meta.name: glmm
meta.intent: Implement Generalized Linear Mixed Models (GLMM) in Rust with equivalent performance to glmmTMB, enabling clinical/epidemiological analyses with random effects (patient, provider, clinic clustering) exposed via WASM to TypeScript
goals: Support random intercepts and slopes with nested and crossed structures
Match glmmTMB coefficient estimates within 1e-4 tolerance
Match glmmTMB standard errors within 1e-3 tolerance
Support all existing GLM families (Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Gamma, InverseGaussian)
Add negative binomial families (nbinom1, nbinom2) required for count data
Expose via WASM with TypeScript bindings matching GLM pattern
Enable DiD analyses with multilevel clustering (patient × provider × clinic)
constraints: Build on existing GLM IRLS infrastructure in packages/dataframe/rust/stats/regression/glm/
Reuse GEE correlation structure patterns from packages/dataframe/rust/stats/regression/gee/
Use Faer 0.22.0 for linear algebra (WASM-compatible, no external deps)
Laplace approximation for random effects integration (matches glmmTMB default)
Sparse Z matrix representation for crossed random effects
Must compile to WASM without additional dependencies

decisions.estimation: Laplace approximation via profile likelihood - matches glmmTMB default, O(1) per random effect vs O(n_quad^q) for AGQ
decisions.optimization: Two-stage: (1) Profile out random effects b given theta, (2) Optimize theta via BFGS/Newton. Inner optimization uses existing IRLS.
decisions.sparseZ: Block-diagonal sparse representation for nested effects, COO format for crossed effects. Dense fallback for small problems (<1000 obs).
decisions.parameterization: Log-Cholesky for variance components (theta = log(sd) and raw correlations) - matches glmmTMB/lme4 parameterization
decisions.families: Extend existing family trait with dispersion parameter support for negative binomial
decisions.blups: Conditional modes from Laplace approximation; standard errors via observed information matrix inversion
decisions.convergence: Relative gradient norm < 1e-6 for outer optimization, IRLS convergence 1e-8 for inner (existing)

build.wasmBuild: pnpm wasmbuild - runs `deno run -A jsr:@deno/wasmbuild@0.19.2 --features wasm --out packages/dataframe/lib`
build.wasmFeatureFlag: All WASM exports must be gated with #[cfg(feature = "wasm")] and use #[wasm_bindgen]
build.typeCheck: pnpm check - must pass before considering implementation complete
build.testGlmm: Add `pnpm test:glmm` script to package.json similar to existing test:glm

wasmIntegrationPattern.step1_rust: Create wasm.rs with #[wasm_bindgen] pub fn glmm_fit_wasm(...) -> String
wasmIntegrationPattern.step2_rust_mod: Export wasm module from glmm/mod.rs, then from regression/mod.rs
wasmIntegrationPattern.step3_rust_root: Add #[cfg(feature = "wasm")] pub use stats::regression::glmm::wasm::* to packages/dataframe/rust/mod.rs
wasmIntegrationPattern.step4_wasmbuild: Run pnpm wasmbuild - generates lib/tidy_ts_dataframe.internal.js with glmm_fit_wasm binding
wasmIntegrationPattern.step5_ts_wrapper: Create packages/dataframe/ts/wasm/glmm-functions.ts that imports {initWasm, wasmInternal} from wasm-init.ts
wasmIntegrationPattern.step6_ts_call: Call initWasm() then wasmInternal.glmm_fit_wasm(formula, family, link, dataJson, optionsJson)
wasmIntegrationPattern.jsonPattern: Data goes in as JSON string, result comes back as JSON string, use encodeWithSpecialFloats/decodeWithSpecialFloats for NaN/Infinity

reusedComponents: glm_fit_core.rs - IRLS algorithm for fixed effects
